title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
description: Discover free social spaces and activities at Biola University, from serene prayer chapels and contemporary art galleries to scenic campus parks and iconic murals.

cards.title: View Contemporary Art
cards.subtitle: Near the Bell Tower
cards.notes: Walk through rotating contemporary art exhibits. It is free for students and visitors; just request a visitor parking pass at the main gatehouse if arriving by car.
cards.short_summary: A campus gallery featuring rotating professional and student contemporary art exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: The Earl & Virginia Green Art Gallery is free for students and outside visitors, though visitors need a free parking pass.
cards.source_title: Visit Us - Art Galleries & Exhibitions - Biola University
cards.access_notes: Open Monday–Friday, 9 a.m.–9 p.m. Visitors need a campus ID for access after 5 p.m.

cards.title: Find Quiet Reflection
cards.subtitle: Near Metzger Hall
cards.notes: Visit the oldest chapel on campus for silent prayer or meditation. It is open to everyone 24/7, providing a reliable space for peace and solitude.
cards.short_summary: A historic, 24-hour prayer chapel dedicated to quiet reflection and individual worship.
cards.evidence_claim: The Rose of Sharon Prayer Chapel is open to students and visitors any time of the day or night, 365 days a year.
cards.source_title: Places for Reflection & Worship - Spiritual Rhythms - Biola University
cards.access_notes: Open 24 hours daily for students and visitors.

cards.title: See the Iconic Mural
cards.subtitle: Science Building Exterior
cards.notes: Observe the 27-foot-tall mural by Kent Twitchell. This public art piece is a central campus landmark and is easily accessible for a quick outdoor visit.
cards.short_summary: A massive, iconic mural of Jesus holding a Bible, located on the exterior of the science building.
cards.evidence_claim: The Jesus Mural, titled 'The Word,' is a prominent piece of public art on the Biola campus science building.
cards.source_title: Contemplations on the Jesus Mural Decision - Biola University
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public art accessible at any time.

cards.entity_name: Fred and Ruth Waugh Prayer Chapel
cards.title: Retreat to Talbot East
cards.subtitle: Talbot East Lower Level
cards.notes: Step into this award-winning architectural space featuring a reclaimed cedar ceiling. It is a quiet, windowless sanctuary perfect for deep focus.
cards.short_summary: A modern, contemplative prayer space in Talbot East known for its unique interior design.
cards.evidence_claim: The Waugh Prayer Chapel in Talbot East is open from 7:30 a.m. to midnight daily for reflection.
cards.source_title: Places for Reflection & Worship - Spiritual Rhythms - Biola University
cards.access_notes: Open daily from 7:30 a.m. to midnight.

cards.title: Walk the Olive Grove
cards.subtitle: Eastern Edge of Campus
cards.notes: Explore the remains of a historic olive orchard. Use the rustic walking paths and benches for an outdoor study session or a quiet break between classes.
cards.short_summary: A peaceful park on the edge of campus featuring historic olive trees and walking paths.
cards.evidence_claim: Kavalich Park, also known as the Olive Grove, features rustic walk paths and benches for the community.
cards.source_title: Places for Reflection & Worship - Spiritual Rhythms - Biola University
cards.access_notes: Publicly accessible outdoor park on campus.

cards.title: Work Out for Free
cards.subtitle: Chase Gymnasium
cards.notes: Current students can access cardio machines and free weights at no extra cost. Bring your valid Biola ID to enter the facility during open hours.
cards.short_summary: The on-campus gym facility providing free fitness resources for the student community.
cards.evidence_claim: The Biola University Fitness Center is free for current students, staff, and faculty with a valid ID.
cards.access_notes: Requires a valid Biola ID and a signed liability waiver.

cards.title: Lounge on the Grass
cards.subtitle: Center of Campus
cards.notes: Gather with friends on the university's largest open green space. It is a popular spot for casual social hangouts, outdoor reading, and campus-wide events.
cards.short_summary: The central hub for outdoor student life and large-scale campus gatherings.
cards.evidence_claim: Metzger Lawn is one of the largest open green-spaces at Biola and serves as a venue for events.
cards.access_notes: Open campus green space accessible to the public.

cards.title: Explore the Garden
cards.subtitle: Near Blackstone Hall
cards.notes: Walk through the campus garden to see seasonal crops like sunflowers and passion fruit. It is a quiet spot to appreciate nature and urban farming efforts.
cards.short_summary: A student-accessible organic garden featuring various fruits, vegetables, and flowers.
cards.evidence_claim: The Biola Organic Garden is a campus space where various crops like sunflowers and passion fruit are grown.
cards.access_notes: Located near Blackstone Hall; generally accessible for viewing.

cards.title: Hike the Creek Trail
cards.subtitle: Santa Gertrudes Avenue
cards.notes: Follow the horse trails and walking paths that connect Biola to this 11-acre city park. It features wooden bridges and an amphitheater for public use.
cards.short_summary: A scenic city park adjacent to campus with trails, bridges, and lush green spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Creek Park is an 11-acre park with walking paths and horse trails that run from the park to Biola University.
cards.source_title: Creek Parks - Discover La Mirada California
cards.access_notes: Public city park open daily from dawn to dusk.

cards.title: Browse Library Art
cards.subtitle: Biola University Library
cards.notes: Check out rotating art displays on the main floor of the library. These exhibits often feature work by students and local community organizations.
cards.short_summary: Rotating art exhibitions hosted within the main floor of the university library.
cards.evidence_claim: Art exhibitions on view throughout the main floor of the University Library feature work by students and local organizations.
cards.access_notes: Accessible during library hours; visitors may need a one-day pass for entry.
